      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0029"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-storage", label: "OCI Object Storage", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_kms_encryption_enforced_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer-Managed Keys (KMS) Encryption on Storage Buckets (Tier-8 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_versioning_enabled_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Object Versioning and Retention Rules for Ransomware Defense (Tier-8 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.versioning
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure versioning for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_emit_events_enabled_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Emit Object Events for Real-Time Security Monitoring (Tier-8 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.object_events_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure object_events_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Object Storage"]
      requirement["Enforce Emit Object Events for Real-Time Security Monitoring"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0032"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-storage", label: "OCI Object Storage", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_public_access_disabled_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Public Access Disabled on OCI Object Storage Buckets (Tier-9 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.access_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_kms_encryption_enforced_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer-Managed Keys (KMS) Encryption on Storage Buckets (Tier-9 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_versioning_enabled_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Object Versioning and Retention Rules for Ransomware Defense (Tier-9 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.versioning
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure versioning for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_emit_events_enabled_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Emit Object Events for Real-Time Security Monitoring (Tier-9 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.object_events_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure object_events_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_public_access_disabled_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Public Access Disabled on OCI Object Storage Buckets (Tier-10 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.access_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_kms_encryption_enforced_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer-Managed Keys (KMS) Encryption on Storage Buckets (Tier-10 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_versioning_enabled_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Object Versioning and Retention Rules for Ransomware Defense (Tier-10 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.versioning
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure versioning for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0039"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-storage", label: "OCI Object Storage", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_emit_events_enabled_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Emit Object Events for Real-Time Security Monitoring (Tier-10 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.object_events_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure object_events_enabled for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

# Rule: Enforce Public Access Disabled on OCI Object Storage Buckets (Tier-11 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.access_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure access_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_kms_encryption_enforced_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Customer-Managed Keys (KMS) Encryption on Storage Buckets (Tier-11 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Object Storage"]
      requirement["Enforce Customer-Managed Keys (KMS) Encryption on Storage Buckets"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0042"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-storage", label: "OCI Object Storage", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_storage.oci_storage_storage_versioning_enabled_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Object Versioning and Retention Rules for Ransomware Defense (Tier-11 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_objectstorage_bucket"
  not r.change.after.versioning
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure versioning for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Object upload and download
developer_guide.contract: Object key, content type, checksum and conditional-write behavior
dependencies: A named bucket or storage account and an application identity
Network and DNS reachability to the object endpoint
Separate read, write and administrative permissions
steps: Provision storage and configure the selected control.
Grant the application only the object operations and paths it needs.
Use the provider SDK credential chain; configure timeouts and bounded retries.
tests: Upload a known payload and compare the downloaded checksum.
Test an unauthorized identity and an object outside the allowed prefix.
Exercise duplicate writes, large objects and retry behavior.
failures: 403: check the data-plane grant, object scope and credential audience.
Timeout: check private DNS, route and endpoint reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_domain_mfa_enforced_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Across All Identity Domain Users
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_domain"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_policy_compartment_scoped_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Least-Privilege IAM Policies with Explicit Compartment Scope
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_policy"
  not r.change.after.statements
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statements for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI IAM"]
      requirement["Enforce Least-Privilege IAM Policies with Explicit Compartment Scope"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0045"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_no_broad_admin_keys_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Prohibit User API Keys with Overbroad Tenancy-Level Administrator Rights
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_api_key"
  not r.change.after.group_memberships
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure group_memberships for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_dynamic_group_instance_principal_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Instance Principals and Dynamic Groups for Compute Workload Auth
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_dynamic_group"
  not r.change.after.matching_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure matching_rule for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_domain_mfa_enforced_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Across All Identity Domain Users (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_domain"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI IAM"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0048"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime

package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_policy_compartment_scoped_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Least-Privilege IAM Policies with Explicit Compartment Scope (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_policy"
  not r.change.after.statements
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statements for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_no_broad_admin_keys_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Prohibit User API Keys with Overbroad Tenancy-Level Administrator Rights (Tier-2 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_api_key"
  not r.change.after.group_memberships
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure group_memberships for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_dynamic_group_instance_principal_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Instance Principals and Dynamic Groups for Compute Workload Auth (Tier-2 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_dynamic_group"
  not r.change.after.matching_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure matching_rule for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_domain_mfa_enforced_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Across All Identity Domain Users (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_domain"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI IAM"]
      requirement["Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Across All Identity Domain Users"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0052"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_policy_compartment_scoped_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Least-Privilege IAM Policies with Explicit Compartment Scope (Tier-3 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_policy"
  not r.change.after.statements
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statements for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_no_broad_admin_keys_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Prohibit User API Keys with Overbroad Tenancy-Level Administrator Rights (Tier-3 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_api_key"
  not r.change.after.group_memberships
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure group_memberships for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_dynamic_group_instance_principal_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Instance Principals and Dynamic Groups for Compute Workload Auth (Tier-3 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_dynamic_group"
  not r.change.after.matching_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure matching_rule for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI IAM"]
      requirement["Configure Instance Principals and Dynamic Groups for Compute Workload Auth"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0055"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_domain_mfa_enforced_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Across All Identity Domain Users (Tier-4 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_domain"
  not r.change.after.mfa_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure mfa_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_iam.oci_iam_iam_policy_compartment_scoped_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Least-Privilege IAM Policies with Explicit Compartment Scope (Tier-4 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_policy"
  not r.change.after.statements
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure statements for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
