package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_shielded_instance_tpm_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM (Tier-5 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.platform_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure platform_config.is_secure_boot_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_disable_public_ip_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances (Tier-5 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.create_vnic_details
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure create_vnic_details.assign_public_ip for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Compute"]
      requirement["Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0147"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-compute", label: "OCI Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_boot_volume_cmk_encryption_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Vault Customer-Managed Encryption on Boot Volumes (Tier-5 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_boot_volume"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_agent_plugins_enabled_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Oracle Cloud Agent Vulnerability and Threat Monitoring Plugins (Tier-5 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.agent_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure agent_config.plugins_config.desired_state for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_shielded_instance_tpm_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM (Tier-6 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.platform_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure platform_config.is_secure_boot_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Compute"]
      requirement["Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0150"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-compute", label: "OCI Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_disable_public_ip_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances (Tier-6 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.create_vnic_details
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure create_vnic_details.assign_public_ip for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_boot_volume_cmk_encryption_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Vault Customer-Managed Encryption on Boot Volumes (Tier-6 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_boot_volume"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_agent_plugins_enabled_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Oracle Cloud Agent Vulnerability and Threat Monitoring Plugins (Tier-6 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.agent_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure agent_config.plugins_config.desired_state for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_shielded_instance_tpm_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM (Tier-7 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.platform_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure platform_config.is_secure_boot_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_disable_public_ip_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances (Tier-7 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.create_vnic_details
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure create_vnic_details.assign_public_ip for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Compute"]
      requirement["Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0155"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-compute", label: "OCI Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_boot_volume_cmk_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Vault Customer-Managed Encryption on Boot Volumes (Tier-7 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_boot_volume"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_agent_plugins_enabled_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Oracle Cloud Agent Vulnerability and Threat Monitoring Plugins (Tier-7 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.agent_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure agent_config.plugins_config.desired_state for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_shielded_instance_tpm_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM (Tier-8 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.platform_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure platform_config.is_secure_boot_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Compute"]
      requirement["Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0158"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-compute", label: "OCI Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_disable_public_ip_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances (Tier-8 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.create_vnic_details
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure create_vnic_details.assign_public_ip for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_boot_volume_cmk_encryption_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Vault Customer-Managed Encryption on Boot Volumes (Tier-8 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_boot_volume"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_agent_plugins_enabled_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Oracle Cloud Agent Vulnerability and Threat Monitoring Plugins (Tier-8 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.agent_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure agent_config.plugins_config.desired_state for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_shielded_instance_tpm_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM (Tier-9 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.platform_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure platform_config.is_secure_boot_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_disable_public_ip_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances (Tier-9 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.create_vnic_details
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure create_vnic_details.assign_public_ip for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Compute"]
      requirement["Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0163"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-compute", label: "OCI Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_boot_volume_cmk_encryption_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Vault Customer-Managed Encryption on Boot Volumes (Tier-9 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_boot_volume"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_agent_plugins_enabled_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Oracle Cloud Agent Vulnerability and Threat Monitoring Plugins (Tier-9 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.agent_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure agent_config.plugins_config.desired_state for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_shielded_instance_tpm_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM (Tier-10 • Profile K)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.platform_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure platform_config.is_secure_boot_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Compute"]
      requirement["Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0166"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-compute", label: "OCI Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_disable_public_ip_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances (Tier-10 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.create_vnic_details
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure create_vnic_details.assign_public_ip for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_boot_volume_cmk_encryption_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Vault Customer-Managed Encryption on Boot Volumes (Tier-10 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_boot_volume"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_agent_plugins_enabled_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Oracle Cloud Agent Vulnerability and Threat Monitoring Plugins (Tier-10 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.agent_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure agent_config.plugins_config.desired_state for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_shielded_instance_tpm_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Compute Instances with Shielded Secure Boot and Measured Boot TPM (Tier-11 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.platform_config
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure platform_config.is_secure_boot_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_disable_public_ip_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances (Tier-11 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_instance"
  not r.change.after.create_vnic_details
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure create_vnic_details.assign_public_ip for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Compute"]
      requirement["Disable Public IP Assignment on Private Compute Subnet Instances"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0171"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-compute", label: "OCI Compute", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_compute.oci_compute_compute_boot_volume_cmk_encryption_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Vault Customer-Managed Encryption on Boot Volumes (Tier-11 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_core_boot_volume"
  not r.change.after.kms_key_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure kms_key_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_database.oci_database_database_private_endpoint_only_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Private Endpoint Only Access on Autonomous Database Instances
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_database_autonomous_database"
  not r.change.after.is_access_control_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure is_access_control_enabled for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_database.oci_database_database_data_safe_registered_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Oracle Data Safe Registration for Automated Security Assessments
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_data_safe_target_database"
  not r.change.after.database_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure database_type for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
