developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_owasp_top_10_rules_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_protection.rules.action_name for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_bot_detection_rate_limit_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Rate Limiting and Challenge-Based Bot Detection on WAF Policy (Tier-2 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_rate_limiting
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_rate_limiting.rules for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_logging_analytics_stream_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Log All WAF Block Actions to Centralized Encrypted Logging Analytics (Tier-2 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_logging_log"
  not r.change.after.log_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure log_type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI WAF"]
      requirement["Log All WAF Block Actions to Centralized Encrypted Logging Analytics"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0352"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-waf", label: "OCI WAF", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_attached_to_load_balancer_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Public Load Balancer Ingress (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall"
  not r.change.after.backend_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backend_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_owasp_top_10_rules_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection (Tier-3 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_protection.rules.action_name for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_bot_detection_rate_limit_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Rate Limiting and Challenge-Based Bot Detection on WAF Policy (Tier-3 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_rate_limiting
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_rate_limiting.rules for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_logging_analytics_stream_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Log All WAF Block Actions to Centralized Encrypted Logging Analytics (Tier-3 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_logging_log"
  not r.change.after.log_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure log_type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI WAF"]
      requirement["Log All WAF Block Actions to Centralized Encrypted Logging Analytics"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0356"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-waf", label: "OCI WAF", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_attached_to_load_balancer_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Public Load Balancer Ingress (Tier-4 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall"
  not r.change.after.backend_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backend_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_owasp_top_10_rules_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection (Tier-4 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_protection.rules.action_name for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_bot_detection_rate_limit_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Rate Limiting and Challenge-Based Bot Detection on WAF Policy (Tier-4 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_rate_limiting
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_rate_limiting.rules for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_logging_analytics_stream_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Log All WAF Block Actions to Centralized Encrypted Logging Analytics (Tier-4 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_logging_log"
  not r.change.after.log_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure log_type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_attached_to_load_balancer_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Public Load Balancer Ingress (Tier-5 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall"
  not r.change.after.backend_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backend_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI WAF"]
      requirement["Enforce OCI Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Public Load Balancer Ingress"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0361"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-waf", label: "OCI WAF", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_owasp_top_10_rules_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection (Tier-5 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_protection.rules.action_name for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_bot_detection_rate_limit_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Rate Limiting and Challenge-Based Bot Detection on WAF Policy (Tier-5 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_rate_limiting
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_rate_limiting.rules for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_logging_analytics_stream_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Log All WAF Block Actions to Centralized Encrypted Logging Analytics (Tier-5 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_logging_log"
  not r.change.after.log_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure log_type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_attached_to_load_balancer_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Public Load Balancer Ingress (Tier-6 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall"
  not r.change.after.backend_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backend_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI WAF"]
      requirement["Enforce OCI Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Public Load Balancer Ingress"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0365"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-waf", label: "OCI WAF", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_owasp_top_10_rules_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection (Tier-6 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_protection.rules.action_name for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_bot_detection_rate_limit_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Rate Limiting and Challenge-Based Bot Detection on WAF Policy (Tier-6 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_rate_limiting
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_rate_limiting.rules for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_logging_analytics_stream_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Log All WAF Block Actions to Centralized Encrypted Logging Analytics (Tier-6 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_logging_log"
  not r.change.after.log_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure log_type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_attached_to_load_balancer_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Public Load Balancer Ingress (Tier-7 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall"
  not r.change.after.backend_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backend_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_owasp_top_10_rules_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection (Tier-7 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_protection.rules.action_name for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI WAF"]
      requirement["Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0370"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-waf", label: "OCI WAF", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_bot_detection_rate_limit_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Rate Limiting and Challenge-Based Bot Detection on WAF Policy (Tier-7 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_rate_limiting
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_rate_limiting.rules for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_logging_analytics_stream_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Log All WAF Block Actions to Centralized Encrypted Logging Analytics (Tier-7 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_logging_log"
  not r.change.after.log_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure log_type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_attached_to_load_balancer_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Public Load Balancer Ingress (Tier-8 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall"
  not r.change.after.backend_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backend_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_owasp_top_10_rules_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection (Tier-8 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_protection.rules.action_name for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI WAF"]
      requirement["Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0374"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-waf", label: "OCI WAF", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_bot_detection_rate_limit_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Rate Limiting and Challenge-Based Bot Detection on WAF Policy (Tier-8 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_rate_limiting
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_rate_limiting.rules for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_logging_analytics_stream_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Log All WAF Block Actions to Centralized Encrypted Logging Analytics (Tier-8 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_logging_log"
  not r.change.after.log_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure log_type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_attached_to_load_balancer_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce OCI Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Public Load Balancer Ingress (Tier-9 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall"
  not r.change.after.backend_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backend_type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_waf.oci_waf_waf_owasp_top_10_rules_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable Protection Rules for OWASP Top 10 Threats and SQL Injection (Tier-9 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_waf_web_app_firewall_policy"
  not r.change.after.request_protection
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure request_protection.rules.action_name for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
