developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_kms.oci_kms_kms_auto_key_rotation_90d_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Automated 90-Day Key Rotation on OCI Vault Master Keys (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_kms_key"
  not r.change.after.auto_key_rotation_details
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_key_rotation_details.rotation_interval_in_days for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_kms.oci_kms_kms_prevent_immediate_key_deletion_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Prohibit Deletion of Master Encryption Keys Without 30-Day Waiting Period (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_kms_key"
  not r.change.after.time_of_deletion
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure time_of_deletion for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Vault KMS"]
      requirement["Prohibit Deletion of Master Encryption Keys Without 30-Day Waiting Period"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0469"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-kms", label: "OCI Vault KMS", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_kms.oci_kms_kms_hsm_dedicated_vault_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Dedicated HSM Vault for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 Cryptographic Keys (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_kms_vault"
  not r.change.after.vault_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vault_type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_kms.oci_kms_kms_auto_key_rotation_90d_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Automated 90-Day Key Rotation on OCI Vault Master Keys (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_kms_key"
  not r.change.after.auto_key_rotation_details
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_key_rotation_details.rotation_interval_in_days for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.

package oracle.oci_kms.oci_kms_kms_prevent_immediate_key_deletion_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Prohibit Deletion of Master Encryption Keys Without 30-Day Waiting Period (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_kms_key"
  not r.change.after.time_of_deletion
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure time_of_deletion for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_kms.oci_kms_kms_hsm_dedicated_vault_t15

default allow = false

# Rule: Deploy Dedicated HSM Vault for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 Cryptographic Keys (Tier-15 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_kms_vault"
  not r.change.after.vault_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vault_type for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Vault KMS"]
      requirement["Deploy Dedicated HSM Vault for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 Cryptographic Keys"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0473"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-kms", label: "OCI Vault KMS", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.

checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_service_connector_stream_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"
  not r.change.after.source
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure source.kind for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

oci iam user get

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "OCI Audit Service", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_service_connector_stream_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"
  not r.change.after.source
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure source.kind for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Audit Service"]
      requirement["Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0481"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "OCI Audit Service", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.

Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

default allow = false

# Rule: Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"
  not r.change.after.source
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure source.kind for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.

checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Audit Service"]
      requirement["Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0486"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "OCI Audit Service", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

deny[msg] {

  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"
  not r.change.after.source
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure source.kind for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table

checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_service_connector_stream_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"
  not r.change.after.source
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure source.kind for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Audit Service"]
      requirement["Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0490"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "OCI Audit Service", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.

failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-7 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_service_connector_stream_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub (Tier-7 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"
  not r.change.after.source
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure source.kind for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Audit Service"]
      requirement["Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0495"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "OCI Audit Service", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.

failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.

  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_service_connector_stream_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"
  not r.change.after.source
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure source.kind for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Audit Service"]
      requirement["Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0499"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "OCI Audit Service", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

A destination and delivery permissions

tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-10 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Audit Service"]
      requirement["Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0504"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "OCI Audit Service", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_service_connector_stream_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"
  not r.change.after.source
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure source.kind for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-11 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_retention_365_days_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce 365-Day Retention for Tenancy-Wide OCI Audit Events (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_audit_policy"
  not r.change.after.retention_period_days
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure retention_period_days for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_service_connector_stream_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_sch_service_connector"
  not r.change.after.source
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure source.kind for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Audit Service"]
      requirement["Stream Audit Logs to External SIEM via OCI Service Connector Hub"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0508"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "OCI Audit Service", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package oracle.oci_audit.oci_audit_audit_alarm_iam_policy_tamper_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Real-time Alarms for Suspicious IAM Policy and Compartment Deletions (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.query
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure query for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
