developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_ons_topic_subscriptions_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Alarms to OCI Notifications (ONS) PagerDuty Subscriptions (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_ons_notification_topic"
  not r.change.after.topic_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure topic_id for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_custom_metrics_ingestion_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable MBean and Custom Telemetry Ingestion from Containerized Microservices (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.namespace
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure namespace for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Monitoring"]
      requirement["Enable MBean and Custom Telemetry Ingestion from Containerized Microservices"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0715"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-monitoring", label: "OCI Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_compute_metric_alarms_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Metric Alarms on Compute High CPU, Memory and Disk Saturation (Tier-10 • Profile B)

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.metric_compartment_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure metric_compartment_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_ons_notification_topic"
  not r.change.after.topic_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure topic_id for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_custom_metrics_ingestion_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable MBean and Custom Telemetry Ingestion from Containerized Microservices (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.namespace
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure namespace for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_compute_metric_alarms_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Metric Alarms on Compute High CPU, Memory and Disk Saturation (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.metric_compartment_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure metric_compartment_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_ons_topic_subscriptions_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Alarms to OCI Notifications (ONS) PagerDuty Subscriptions (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_ons_notification_topic"
  not r.change.after.topic_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure topic_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review

    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-monitoring", label: "OCI Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }

    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]

      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.namespace
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure namespace for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_compute_metric_alarms_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Metric Alarms on Compute High CPU, Memory and Disk Saturation (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.metric_compartment_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure metric_compartment_id for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_ons_topic_subscriptions_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Alarms to OCI Notifications (ONS) PagerDuty Subscriptions (Tier-12 • Profile I)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_ons_notification_topic"
  not r.change.after.topic_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure topic_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_custom_metrics_ingestion_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable MBean and Custom Telemetry Ingestion from Containerized Microservices (Tier-12 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.namespace
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure namespace for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Monitoring"]
      requirement["Enable MBean and Custom Telemetry Ingestion from Containerized Microservices"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0724"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-monitoring", label: "OCI Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_ons_topic_subscriptions_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Alarms to OCI Notifications (ONS) PagerDuty Subscriptions (Tier-13 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_ons_notification_topic"
  not r.change.after.topic_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure topic_id for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_custom_metrics_ingestion_t13

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable MBean and Custom Telemetry Ingestion from Containerized Microservices (Tier-13 • Profile M)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.namespace
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure namespace for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_compute_metric_alarms_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Metric Alarms on Compute High CPU, Memory and Disk Saturation (Tier-14 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.metric_compartment_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure metric_compartment_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_ons_topic_subscriptions_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Route High-Severity Alarms to OCI Notifications (ONS) PagerDuty Subscriptions (Tier-14 • Profile O)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_ons_notification_topic"
  not r.change.after.topic_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure topic_id for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_custom_metrics_ingestion_t14

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable MBean and Custom Telemetry Ingestion from Containerized Microservices (Tier-14 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.namespace
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure namespace for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_monitoring.oci_monitoring_monitoring_compute_metric_alarms_t15

default allow = false

# Rule: Configure Metric Alarms on Compute High CPU, Memory and Disk Saturation (Tier-15 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_monitoring_alarm"
  not r.change.after.metric_compartment_id
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure metric_compartment_id for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_host_scan_recipe_enabled_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI Vulnerability Scanning Service (VSS) on All Compute Hosts
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.schedule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schedule.type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_container_scan_recipe_enabled_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI VSS Container Image Scanning on Pushed Repositories in OCIR
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_container_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.image_count
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure image_count for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Vulnerability Scanning"]
      requirement["Enable OCI VSS Container Image Scanning on Pushed Repositories in OCIR"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0733"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-vulnerability", label: "OCI Vulnerability Scanning", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_zero_critical_cve_gate_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Zero High/Critical CVE Policy Prior to Deployment in Production
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_target"
  not r.change.after.description
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure description for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Vulnerability Scanning"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0734"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-vulnerability", label: "OCI Vulnerability Scanning", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_host_scan_recipe_enabled_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI Vulnerability Scanning Service (VSS) on All Compute Hosts (Tier-2 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.schedule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schedule.type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_container_scan_recipe_enabled_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI VSS Container Image Scanning on Pushed Repositories in OCIR (Tier-2 • Profile E)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_container_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.image_count
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure image_count for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_zero_critical_cve_gate_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Zero High/Critical CVE Policy Prior to Deployment in Production (Tier-2 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_target"
  not r.change.after.description
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure description for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Vulnerability Scanning"]
      requirement["Enforce Zero High/Critical CVE Policy Prior to Deployment in Production"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0737"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-vulnerability", label: "OCI Vulnerability Scanning", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.

Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_host_scan_recipe_enabled_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI Vulnerability Scanning Service (VSS) on All Compute Hosts (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.schedule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schedule.type for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}

tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_container_scan_recipe_enabled_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI VSS Container Image Scanning on Pushed Repositories in OCIR (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_container_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.image_count
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure image_count for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_zero_critical_cve_gate_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Zero High/Critical CVE Policy Prior to Deployment in Production (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_target"
  not r.change.after.description
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure description for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Vulnerability Scanning"]
      requirement["Enforce Zero High/Critical CVE Policy Prior to Deployment in Production"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0740"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-vulnerability", label: "OCI Vulnerability Scanning", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_host_scan_recipe_enabled_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI Vulnerability Scanning Service (VSS) on All Compute Hosts (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.schedule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schedule.type for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}

dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_container_scan_recipe_enabled_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI VSS Container Image Scanning on Pushed Repositories in OCIR (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_container_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.image_count
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure image_count for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_zero_critical_cve_gate_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Zero High/Critical CVE Policy Prior to Deployment in Production (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_target"
  not r.change.after.description
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure description for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_host_scan_recipe_enabled_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI Vulnerability Scanning Service (VSS) on All Compute Hosts (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.schedule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schedule.type for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_container_scan_recipe_enabled_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI VSS Container Image Scanning on Pushed Repositories in OCIR (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_container_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.image_count
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure image_count for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_zero_critical_cve_gate_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Zero High/Critical CVE Policy Prior to Deployment in Production (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_target"
  not r.change.after.description
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure description for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Vulnerability Scanning"]

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0746"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-vulnerability", label: "OCI Vulnerability Scanning", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource

    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_host_scan_recipe_enabled_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI Vulnerability Scanning Service (VSS) on All Compute Hosts (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.schedule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure schedule.type for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Vulnerability Scanning"]
      requirement["Enable OCI Vulnerability Scanning Service (VSS) on All Compute Hosts"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0747"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-vulnerability", label: "OCI Vulnerability Scanning", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_container_scan_recipe_enabled_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enable OCI VSS Container Image Scanning on Pushed Repositories in OCIR (Tier-6 • Profile Q)

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_container_scan_recipe"
  not r.change.after.image_count
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure image_count for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify artifact digest, trusted signer identity, and relevant attestations
An image signature establishes provenance only under the configured trust policy. Scan results, deployment admission, and runtime restrictions remain separate controls.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_vulnerability.oci_vulnerability_vss_zero_critical_cve_gate_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Zero High/Critical CVE Policy Prior to Deployment in Production (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_vulnerability_scanning_host_scan_target"
  not r.change.after.description
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure description for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Vulnerability Scanning"]
      requirement["Enforce Zero High/Critical CVE Policy Prior to Deployment in Production"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0749"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-vulnerability", label: "OCI Vulnerability Scanning", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
