developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-3 • Profile G)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup

    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_compartments_hierarchy_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries (Tier-3 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_compartment"
  not r.change.after.enable_delete
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enable_delete for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]
      requirement["Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0997"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_budget_alert_rules_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds (Tier-3 • Profile I)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_budget_budget"
  not r.change.after.alert_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_rule.threshold for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-4 • Profile J)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-0999"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_compartments_hierarchy_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries (Tier-4 • Profile K)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_compartment"
  not r.change.after.enable_delete
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enable_delete for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1000"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end

      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_budget_alert_rules_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds (Tier-4 • Profile L)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_budget_budget"
  not r.change.after.alert_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_rule.threshold for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]
      requirement["Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1001"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-5 • Profile M)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_compartments_hierarchy_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries (Tier-5 • Profile N)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_compartment"
  not r.change.after.enable_delete
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enable_delete for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_budget_alert_rules_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds (Tier-5 • Profile O)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_budget_budget"
  not r.change.after.alert_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_rule.threshold for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-6 • Profile P)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]
      requirement["Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1005"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_compartments_hierarchy_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries (Tier-6 • Profile Q)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_compartment"
  not r.change.after.enable_delete
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enable_delete for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_budget_alert_rules_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds (Tier-6 • Profile R)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_budget_budget"
  not r.change.after.alert_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_rule.threshold for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      requirement --> check

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-7 • Profile S)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]
      requirement["Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1008"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_compartments_hierarchy_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries (Tier-7 • Profile T)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_compartment"
  not r.change.after.enable_delete
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enable_delete for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_budget_alert_rules_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds (Tier-7 • Profile U)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_budget_budget"
  not r.change.after.alert_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_rule.threshold for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-8 • Profile V)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]
      requirement["Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1011"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_compartments_hierarchy_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries (Tier-8 • Profile W)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_compartment"
  not r.change.after.enable_delete
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enable_delete for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB

      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1012"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource

    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_budget_alert_rules_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds (Tier-8 • Profile X)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_budget_budget"
  not r.change.after.alert_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_rule.threshold for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-9 • Profile Y)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1014"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_compartments_hierarchy_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries (Tier-9 • Profile Z)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_compartment"
  not r.change.after.enable_delete
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enable_delete for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]
      requirement["Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1015"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_budget_alert_rules_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds (Tier-9 • Profile A)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_budget_budget"
  not r.change.after.alert_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_rule.threshold for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-10 • Profile B)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1017"]
      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review
    end

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_compartments_hierarchy_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries (Tier-10 • Profile C)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_compartment"
  not r.change.after.enable_delete
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enable_delete for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_budget_alert_rules_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds (Tier-10 • Profile D)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_budget_budget"
  not r.change.after.alert_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_rule.threshold for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-11 • Profile E)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.2.1, NIST 800-53 AU-2, SOC 2 Type II CC6.8
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_compartments_hierarchy_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries (Tier-11 • Profile F)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_compartment"
  not r.change.after.enable_delete
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure enable_delete for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]
      requirement["Structure Compartments Hierarchy Following Least-Privilege Trust Boundaries"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1021"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_budget_alert_rules_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds (Tier-11 • Profile G)
# Compliance: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0, NIST 800-53 SC-13, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4, SOC 2 CC6.1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_budget_budget"
  not r.change.after.alert_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure alert_rule.threshold for compliance standard CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v2.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Oracle Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for OCI Governance & Compartments"]
      requirement["Enforce Budget Alerts on Tenancy and Compartment Cost Thresholds"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:oci-iam", label: "OCI IAM policy and compartment authorization", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: OCI-BP-1022"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Oracle Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:oci-audit", label: "Supported OCI Audit events and Cloud Guard problems", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Policy evaluation at resource administration boundaries
developer_guide.contract: Principal, requested action, resource scope and applicable policy effect
dependencies: A resource hierarchy and explicitly scoped policy assignments
A separate administrative identity and a test environment
steps: Stage policy changes at a limited scope.
Test a permitted request and a request the policy should reject.
Review inherited assignments and rollout effects before widening scope.
tests: Verify policy denial and a known allowed administration path.
Check whether an existing resource needs separate remediation.
failures: Unexpected denial: inspect inherited policy scope and exclusions.
No enforcement: inspect policy effect and service applicability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
oci iam user get
: "${COMPARTMENT_OCID:?Set COMPARTMENT_OCID to target compartment}"
oci compute instance list --compartment-id "$COMPARTMENT_OCID" --output table
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package oracle.oci_governance.oci_governance_governance_tag_defaults_enforced_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Enforce Defined Tag Defaults Across All New Compartment Resources (Tier-12 • Profile H)
# Compliance: CIS OCI 2.1.0, NIST SP 800-171, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv), FedRAMP High
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "oci_identity_tag_default"
  not r.change.after.value
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure value for compliance standard CIS OCI 2.1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource in OCI Console / OCI CLI or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review
    end

      resource@{ icon: "logos:oci-governance", label: "OCI Governance & Compartments", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
